questions.q: Why is saving only `model.state_dict()` usually not enough to resume training cleanly?
options: model.state_dict() cannot be saved with torch.save at all
It omits optimizer and scheduler state, like Adam's running averages and the scheduler's decay position, which restart from scratch otherwise
It only works for models with no convolutional layers
model.state_dict() already includes the optimizer state automatically
questions.explain: Weights alone are enough for inference, but the optimizer's per-parameter running statistics and the scheduler's position in its decay curve are also needed to truly resume training where it left off.

options: It changes the model's architecture to match the device
It remaps which device the loaded tensors are placed on, e.g. loading a GPU-saved checkpoint onto a CPU or a different GPU
It deletes the optimizer state before loading
It forces weights_only=True
questions.explain: map_location tells torch.load which device to place the restored tensors on, letting a checkpoint saved on one device (e.g. a GPU) be loaded cleanly on another (e.g. CPU, or a different GPU index).

questions.q: Why does this lesson's checkpoint-loading code pass `weights_only=False` to `torch.load`?
options: Because the checkpoint file is corrupted
Because the checkpoint dictionary contains more than tensors — optimizer and scheduler state and other metadata — and the safer default rejects that
Because weights_only=False speeds up loading
Because model.state_dict() requires it even for inference-only loading
questions.explain: torch.load's weights_only=True default is a safety measure that only allows loading plain tensors. A checkpoint that also bundles optimizer/scheduler state dicts needs weights_only=False to load, and should only be used on files you trust.

questions.q: In the resumable training loop pattern shown in this lesson, what determines `start_epoch`?
options: It is always hardcoded to 0
The saved checkpoint's `epoch` value plus one
A random value chosen at runtime
The current learning rate
questions.explain: The checkpoint stores the last completed epoch number; resuming sets start_epoch to that stored value plus one so training continues with the next epoch.

questions.q: What is a common checkpointing pattern mentioned in this lesson for managing saved files during a long run?
options: Save a checkpoint only once, at the very end of training
Keep both a 'latest' checkpoint (to resume from) and a separate 'best' checkpoint (saved whenever validation loss improves)
Never save the optimizer state, only the model weights
Delete all checkpoints as soon as training finishes
questions.explain: A common pattern saves a 'latest' checkpoint every epoch (or every N steps) to resume from after an interruption, plus a separate 'best' checkpoint whenever validation performance improves.
